posters.title: Every work. Every material. One page.
posters.body: V11 groups {{works}} works into {{areas}} areas. Each work has its materials immediately underneath it. All {{materials}} material lines are visible, with search, area filters and same-page jumps.
posters.takeaway: Ask for open work sections with embedded material tables.

posters.title: Name the shape.
posters.body: These phrases describe the layout you wanted:
posters.takeaway: “All details inline” is the useful phrase.

posters.title: One source. Different views.
posters.body: V9 holds the published data. V10 and v11 present it in different ways.
posters.takeaway: A committed source change rebuilds the linked pages. Browser edits remain a local contractor draft shared by v10 and v11.

posters.title: Quantity × rate = amount.
posters.body: Match the purchase unit on both sides of the calculation. A price per sheet needs a quantity in sheets.
posters.takeaway: Work area in m² and a purchase count in sheets are different measurements.

posters.title: Unknown ≠ zero.
posters.body: A blank quantity still needs a take-off. An unpriced material still needs a supplier quote. A partial subtotal includes only the priced rows.
items: {{held}} held works keep their original values
Original quote currency and component splits need confirmation
posters.takeaway: Confirm measurements, specification, taxes and delivery before ordering.

posters.title: Give the goal and the shape.
posters.body: A useful request tells me five things:
items: Rules · units, unknowns and held values
Finish · verify, publish and send the link
posters.takeaway: State what the contractor should see and do.

posters.title: “Put the detail on the same page.”
posters.body: This is the prompt that would have described v11 clearly.
posters.prompt:
Create v11 as a derived view of v10 in our CAD_Test-Facility repository. Preserve v10 and every earlier version.

Put every work on one page, grouped by area, with an open section for each work. Directly underneath each work, show its materials in a four-column table:
Material / specification | Required quantity + purchase unit | Unit rate (NPR) | Amount (NPR).

Keep quantities, rates, calculations and contractor browser drafts linked to v10. Show all works and material rows by default. Add same-page search, area filters, work jumps and printing. Allow quantities, selected specifications and supplier prices to be edited inline.

Preserve SI work units, Indian number formatting, zero values, unknown measurements/prices, {{held}} held works and {{allowances}} unsplit allowances. Label public prices as references and partial totals as partial. Keep mobile layouts and light/dark modes.

Verify the calculations and links, publish through our GitHub Actions/Pages workflow, and send me the working v11 link.
posters.takeaway: Goal + source + page structure + data rules + publication.

posters.title: Change the view, keep the source.
posters.prompt: Update [version] so a contractor can [task]. Use [open sections / compact tables / another named layout] with at most [number] columns. Derive its values from the existing shared source and calculations. Preserve existing versions, prices, quantities, unknowns and held values. Keep the page readable on desktop and mobile. Verify, publish and send the working link.
posters.takeaway: Name the view, the task and the layout you want.

posters.title: Ask for evidence with the price.
posters.prompt: For [work / material], update the shared source using current Kathmandu supplier evidence. Record the material specification, purchase unit, unit rate or range, source link and date, and stated tax/delivery basis. Determine the required quantity from the work measurement and explicit take-off assumptions. Leave unresolved inputs unknown. Rebuild all dependent views, preserve historical evidence and held works, and report the remaining gaps.
posters.takeaway: A useful price has a unit, a specification and a source.

posters.title: Freeze a reviewable result.
posters.prompt: Tag and release the current verified website as a new milestone. Keep earlier tags and releases fixed. Include the implemented features, source dependencies, checks and remaining limitations in the release notes. Tag the exact commit after its tests and Pages deployment succeed. Give me the live website and GitHub release links.
posters.takeaway: A release records a specific commit; it does not confirm supplier inputs.

posters.title: Leave room for the next good idea.
posters.prompt: Add a Memory Poster about [topic] under [category]. Give it a short title, one useful explanation, a concrete example, a reusable prompt and a source link where relevant. Keep the main content visible, readable in light/dark modes and printable. Add it to the existing poster collection and preserve the other posters.
posters.takeaway: This wall can grow through its shared poster collection.
